newsitem.title: UK: Livestock farmers may use more feed wheat -IGC.
newsitem.headline: Livestock farmers may use more feed wheat -IGC.

text.p: As wheat prices tumble, livestock farmers across the world may turn to wheat for animal feeding, the International Grains Council (IGC) said in a report on Thursday.
"More wheat of feed quality is likely to be available on international markets than last season," said the London-based Council in its latest monthly review of grain markets.
"Some of the big EU (European Union) crop may be exported for feed and wet weather recently in the northern Prairies will reduce some of Canada's harvest to feed quality," it said.
Already feed wheat is priced at level with feed barley in some EU member states.
The IGC said feed wheat from several exporters would also compete strongly with maize for livestock feeding.
The key issue is how much feed wheat Korea will import this season.

Korea is the world's biggest importer of feed wheat and the IGC said it could use at least 1.5 million tonnes of wheat for feed in the 1996/97 (July/June) season, one million tonnes more than the previous season.
Central and Eastern European countries could also import some feed wheat as unfavourable weather and insufficient inputs have resulted in lower harvests this year.
The IGC raised its estimate for Central and Eastern European wheat imports to 2.1 million tonnes from 1.1 million tonnes in 1995/96.
"There will be a lot of feed wheat around," said Bill De Maria, assistant executive director of the IGC.
